basics.description: Deploys FHIRBridge (portal + API), the Demo app, and their supporting SQL Server Express, Redis, and background Worker into a single Azure Container Apps environment in this subscription.

location.label: Region
location.toolTip: All resources in this deployment are created in this region.

basics.name: namePrefix
basics.label: Deployment name prefix
basics.toolTip: Short name used to build every resource name in this deployment (e.g. <prefix>-app, <prefix>-sqlserver).

constraints.validationMessage: Lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only, starting with a letter.

elements.name: sqlSaPassword
elements.toolTip: Password for the SQL Server Express container's sa account. Must satisfy SQL Server's complexity policy (8+ chars, upper/lower/digit/symbol).

constraints.validationMessage: At least 8 characters, including upper case, lower case, and a digit.

elements.name: jwtSigningKey
elements.toolTip: FHIRBridge.Api's Authentication:SigningKey (HS256) — used to sign access/refresh tokens. At least 32 random characters; treat it like a secret.

elements.name: redisPassword
elements.toolTip: Password Redis requires to connect (--requirepass) — defense-in-depth on top of network isolation.

elements.name: sqlServerSize
elements.label: SQL Server size
elements.toolTip: SQL Server's first-run setup can need more headroom than steady-state — pick XLarge if it fails to initialize on Large.

elements.name: redisSize
elements.label: Redis size
elements.toolTip: Redis's own cache/queue memory needs — separate from the data it persists to its file share.

elements.name: fhirbridgeAppSize
elements.label: FHIRBridge app size
elements.toolTip: Runs both FHIRBridge.Api and FHIRBridge.Gateway in this one container.

elements.name: workerSize
elements.label: Worker size
elements.toolTip: Background scheduler/pipeline processor — no HTTP endpoint.

elements.name: imageTag
elements.label: Version to install
elements.toolTip: The published version tag to deploy (see the vendor registry's release list for available versions).

options.text: Optional — leave everything blank to just use the default *.azurecontainerapps.io URLs. Setting a domain here is a 3-step flow, done entirely by redeploying this same wizard, no CLI/portal action needed: (1) deploy once with these left blank, find the fhirbridgeAppDomainVerificationId / demoAppDomainVerificationId outputs on this deployment afterward, add a CNAME (your domain -> the matching *Url output's hostname) and a TXT record (asuid.<your domain>) at your DNS provider using the verification output, wait for DNS to propagate; (2) come back, fill in the domain(s) below with the SSL checkbox(es) still OFF, and redeploy — this registers the domain with no certificate yet (reachable, not secured); (3) once the TXT record is confirmed in place, come back again, turn the matching SSL checkbox ON, and redeploy — this is the step that actually validates the TXT record and issues + binds the free managed certificate, failing cleanly (safe to retry) if DNS isn't ready yet.

elements.name: fhirbridgeAppCustomDomain
elements.label: FHIRBridge app custom domain
elements.toolTip: e.g. app.customer.com. Leave blank to keep the default *.azurecontainerapps.io URL.

elements.name: fhirbridgeAppSslEnabled
elements.label: Issue + bind SSL certificate for the FHIRBridge app domain (step 3)
elements.toolTip: Leave OFF until the asuid.<domain> TXT record is confirmed in place (step 2 already redeployed with the domain above). Turning this ON and redeploying is what actually requests and binds the free managed certificate. Has no effect while the domain above is blank.

elements.name: demoAppCustomDomain
elements.label: Demo app custom domain
elements.toolTip: e.g. demo.customer.com. Leave blank to keep the default *.azurecontainerapps.io URL.

elements.name: demoAppSslEnabled
elements.label: Issue + bind SSL certificate for the Demo app domain (step 3)
elements.toolTip: Same idea as the FHIRBridge app's SSL checkbox above, for the demo app's own domain.

options.text:
This deployment creates 12 new resources in the selected resource group, and nothing outside it:

• 5 Container Apps — SQL Server Express, Redis, FHIRBridge (Api + Gateway), Demo App, Worker
• 1 Container Apps Environment hosting all 5
• 1 Log Analytics workspace (required by Container Apps for logs/metrics — not optional)
• 1 Storage Account with 2 Azure File shares (persistent data for SQL Server and Redis)

SQL Server and Redis are reachable only from the other apps in this environment, never the public internet. The full list of resource IDs this deployment creates is also saved as a 'resourceManifest' output on the deployment itself, viewable afterward under this deployment's history — that exact list is what the cleanup script uses to tear this down precisely later.
Double-check the values on the previous steps, then continue to "Review + create" to see the final parameter summary before anything is actually deployed.
